title: Close an account without leaving readable stale bytes
prompt: Add a `CloseCounter` instruction that closes a counter account and returns its lamports to the counter's recorded authority. Compliance requires that nothing readable is left in the account data after closing — a later rent payer must not be able to inspect old counter bytes. Only the authority recorded in the counter may close it. Keep everything building.
expectation: The erasure requirement selects `CloseAccountZeroed` over `CloseAccount`. The agent validates the counter's authority (signer plus stored-authority match) before closing, routes lamports to that authority, and does not hand-roll lamport transfer plus data truncation — the close builders own that sequence, including the zero-before-transfer ordering.

checks.why: The requirement rules out the plain close builder: stale counter bytes must not remain observable.
Using the non-zeroing builder would leave the old counter bytes readable.

Only the recorded authority may close; the signer check must sit inside the close handler (whatever the agent names it, `CloseCounter` or `Close`) and precede the close. File-wide matching would let the `Increment` and `Reset` handlers satisfy it on a close handler that skips the check.
A signer check alone proves nothing about which counter; the stored authority must bind inside the same handler before lamports move.
Hand-rolled zero-then-transfer duplicates the builder and can reorder it wrongly.
The public surface changed, so the snapshot gate must still pass.
The close builder is type-checked against the account type.
